index.heroParagraph: Fabulous Nothing is the blank-slate preset that ships with Fabulous Factory — scaffolded with one npx command, not cloned from a template. This page is about the factory.

auth.sourceCaption: Example — what you'll write, once you add an auth-gated action

jobs.whatItDoesBody: From a caller's side: @factory/jobs is one Inngest client and one function registry, nothing more — no pipeline or run-engine abstraction ships with this preset. Scaffold a job with pnpm gen job <name>, register it, and it runs on Inngest Cloud or a local dev server identically, whichever is configured.
jobs.ruleBody: Every registered function shares the same client, so INNGEST_EVENT_KEY/INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY/INNGEST_DEV govern all of them identically — there is no per-job env wiring to get wrong. The Inngest SDK itself stays confined to this package (and to any domain package that ships its own functions, e.g. the Untangle preset's packages/untangle) — never a direct import anywhere else, boundary-enforced by pnpm boundaries.
jobs.realSourceBody: The module-scope client every registered function is built against:
jobs.workingExampleBody: This preset ships with no functions registered yet — the registry below is a literal empty array until your first pnpm gen job, so instead of a fake run, here is exactly what that scaffold-and-register flow changes.
jobs.registryLiveExampleTitle: The registry, before and after your first job
jobs.registryCaption: packages/jobs/src/functions/index.ts — the registry pnpm gen job populates
jobs.turnItOnBody: Point the app at Inngest Cloud with the two key vars, or run a local dev server with INNGEST_DEV=1. Without either, whatever functions you register simply don't fire — nothing else in this preset depends on Inngest being configured.

llm.exampleIntro: A live call here would spend money on anonymous traffic, and this preset ships with no feature that calls it yet — so instead of a fake button, here is the exact contract a caller gets back on every element, taken straight from the snippet above.

billing.exampleIntro: Set both Stripe keys and checkout and webhooks switch on together. Leave them unset and every account gets runsPerDay: null — unlimited, subject only to the fixed, per-day abuse ceiling every profile enforces.
billing.exampleOutro: This preset ships no billing card yet — getEntitlement() is the one call a paywalled feature needs to check a plan limit, whichever way you choose to render it. With Stripe configured, an upgrade raises that limit the moment the webhook lands.

observability.closingNote: This preset ships no feature that calls track() yet — once one does, set both keys and it starts reporting; unset them and the same call sites keep running exactly the same, just quietly doing nothing.

degradationStrip.heading: Unset the LLM key and nothing breaks
degradationStrip.body: Same call, same call site, either way. With a key, streamArray() and generate() do their work. Without one, they throw before any provider SDK ever loads — and every call site in the template is written to catch that and fall back to a non-AI result rather than let it reach a user.
